sectors.name: Silicon
sectors.blurb: Who designs the chips, who makes them, who supplies the memory and who sells the machines that print them.

rows.name: AI accelerators
rows.metric: Nvidia Data Center revenue of $89.0bn in the quarter to 26 Jul 2026, up 117% year on year. Estimates of Nvidia's share of AI accelerator revenue run from about 70% to over 80%, depending on whether in-house chips are counted.

rows.name: Custom chips for the biggest buyers
rows.metric: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7bn in the quarter to 2 Aug 2026, up 221% year on year. Guide for the next quarter is $21.7bn.

rows.name: CPUs and architecture
rows.metric: x86 unit share, Q2 2026 (Mercury Research, as reported): Intel 69.3%, AMD 30.7%. Intel fell below 70% for the first time since 1995.

rows.name: Foundries
rows.metric: Share of top-ten foundry revenue, 2Q26 (TrendForce): TSMC 72.5%, Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%, UMC 3.9%, GlobalFoundries 3.2%. Top ten together: $53.49bn.

rows.name: Memory
rows.metric: DRAM share, Q2 2026 (Counterpoint): Samsung 38%, SK hynix 25 to 26%, Micron 24 to 25%, CXMT about 10%. HBM: SK hynix about 50%, Samsung about 33%, Micron about 18%.

rows.name: Chip equipment
rows.metric: ASML net sales of EUR 9.3bn in Q2 2026. Full-year 2026 guide EUR 43 to 45bn, with about 65 low-NA EUV systems to ship. ASML, Applied Materials, Lam, Tokyo Electron and KLA were the top five in 2025 (TechInsights).

sectors.name: Infrastructure and data centers
sectors.blurb: The networks, storage, servers, buildings, money and power that turn chips into AI capacity.

rows.name: Networking
rows.metric: Ethernet is about two-thirds of AI cluster switch sales (Q1 2026), up from under 20% in late 2023. Celestica and Nvidia led 2025 with a combined 50% share. In 2Q26 Celestica led Ethernet AI back-end switch sales, Nvidia was close behind, Arista third and Cisco fourth and gaining the most share (Dell'Oro).

rows.name: Storage
rows.metric: No audited share figure exists for AI storage. VAST Data raised $1bn at a $30bn valuation in April 2026 (reported). DDN took $300m at $5bn in January 2025 (Blackstone). Pure Storage, now Everpure, reported $3.7bn of fiscal 2026 revenue.

rows.name: Servers and systems
rows.metric: Server revenue share, Q1 2026 (IDC): Dell 16.5% on $20.28bn, Super Micro 7.6%, Lenovo 4.6%, IEIT 3.3%, HPE 3%. Unbranded ODM direct supply, where Foxconn, Quanta and Wistron sit, was 50.2% of revenue.

rows.name: Data center landlords and financiers
rows.metric: Equinix Q2 2026 revenue of $2.63bn and record annualized bookings of $424m, up 23%. Digital Realty reported a record $1.9bn backlog (100% share). Blackstone projects 7 GW of data center leasing across its platforms in 2026.

rows.name: Power and cooling
rows.metric: GE Vernova's backlog stood at $176bn at the end of Q2 2026, with gas turbine slot reservations at 56 GW. Vertiv's trailing orders grew 81% organically. Bloom Energy's backlog was reported near $6bn, up 140%.

sectors.name: Cloud and compute
sectors.blurb: Who rents out the computers, and who is catching up by renting only the AI ones.

rows.name: Public cloud
rows.metric: Share of cloud infrastructure spending, Q2 2026 (Synergy Research, as reported): Amazon 28%, Microsoft 20%, Google 15%, in a market of about $143bn. Other trackers give different splits.

rows.name: GPU clouds and inference platforms
rows.metric: CoreWeave revenue of $2.575bn in Q2 2026, more than double a year earlier, with a revenue backlog of about $104bn at 30 June. 2026 revenue guide $12.4bn to $13.2bn.

sectors.name: AI models and platforms
sectors.blurb: The labs that build the models and the apps that sell them.

rows.name: Frontier labs
rows.metric: Enterprise LLM API spend, late 2025 (Menlo Ventures survey of 495 US decision makers, excluding consumer revenue): Anthropic about 40%, OpenAI 27%, Google 21%. Ramp's August 2026 data shows 43.8% of US businesses paying Anthropic and 39.8% paying OpenAI.

sectors.name: Software
sectors.blurb: The applications companies run on, and the argument over whether agents break the seat-based business.

rows.name: Enterprise applications
rows.metric: 2026 repriced software on the fear that AI agents reduce per-seat demand. Commentators put the February selloff at about $285bn, with one measure of the sector down more than 23% for the year to date. Vendors are moving to usage and per-action pricing.

rows.name: Data and analytics
rows.metric: Databricks reported a $7bn revenue run rate in Q2 2026, growing more than 80%, and closed $5bn at a $190bn valuation in August 2026. Snowflake's fiscal Q1 2027 product revenue was $1.334bn, up 34%. Palantir's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.935bn, up 92.8% (reported).

rows.name: Developer tools and observability
rows.metric: Datadog's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.12bn, up 36%, with 33,400 customers and remaining performance obligations of $3.47bn, up 43%. GitHub Copilot is reported at 50 million users.

sectors.name: Security
sectors.blurb: Who defends the systems, and who is buying the pieces to build one platform.

rows.name: Security platforms
rows.metric: Palo Alto Networks' next-generation security ARR was $9.10bn at the end of fiscal 2026, up 63%, including $1.6bn from CyberArk and Chronosphere. CrowdStrike's ending ARR was about $5.84bn, up 25%. Zscaler's ARR was $3.771bn, up 25%.

rows.name: Cloud, identity and data security
rows.metric: Google completed its Wiz purchase on 11 March 2026 at a price of about $29.5bn after adjustments (Alphabet 10-Q). Palo Alto Networks closed its roughly $25bn CyberArk purchase on 11 February 2026. Okta's fiscal Q2 2027 revenue was $805m, up 11%.

sectors.name: Internet and consumer platforms
sectors.blurb: Where the money is collected: ads, subscriptions, commerce and games.

rows.name: Search, social and advertising
rows.metric: Google was about 89.9% of global search referral traffic in September 2026 (StatCounter, which measures referrals and not searches). Q2 2026 advertising revenue: Google about $82bn (+14%), Meta $59.36bn (+27%), Amazon $19.8bn (+26%), YouTube $11.1bn (+12.9%) (secondary reports).

rows.name: Video and streaming
rows.metric: Nielsen's Gauge for July 2026: streaming was 49.0% of US TV time, with YouTube at a record 14.2%, Disney's streaming services 4.7% combined and Peacock 2.6%. In June, Netflix was 7.9% and Prime Video 4.2%.

rows.name: Commerce platforms
rows.metric: Shopify's gross merchandise volume was $115.6bn in Q2 2026, up 32%, on revenue of $3.6bn, up 34% (10-Q). Amazon's net sales were $200.6bn, up 20%.

rows.name: Games
rows.metric: Tencent's domestic games revenue was RMB 47.3bn in Q2 2026, up 17%, and international games RMB 18.6bn, down 0.8%. Roblox bookings grew 8% to about $1.6bn with 123 million daily users.

sectors.name: Devices
sectors.blurb: The phones, laptops and glasses people carry, all squeezed by the same memory shortage.

rows.name: Smartphones
rows.metric: Q2 2026 shipments of 276.3 million, down 7.4% (IDC). Samsung 62.7m and 22.7% share, Apple 55.7m and 20.2%, Xiaomi about 11.3%, OPPO 10.4%, vivo 7.6%. IDC expects 2026 shipments to fall 16.7% to just over 1bn, the steepest annual drop on record.

rows.name: PCs
rows.metric: Q2 2026 PC shipments of 68.2 million, down 4.9% (IDC). Lenovo 24.4%, HP 19.1%, Dell 13.6% and Apple 9.9%. Counterpoint puts the decline at 4%, and IDC expects the DRAM shortage to last into early 2028.

rows.name: Smart glasses and XR
rows.metric: XR and smart glasses shipments grew about 35% in Q2 2026 (IDC), down from 130% in the prior quarter. Glasses are nearly 85% of XR shipments and headsets about 15%. Meta's share of smart glasses is put at 69% to 76% depending on the source.

sectors.name: Fintech and payments
sectors.blurb: Who moves the money, who is replacing the bank account and who issues the digital dollar.

rows.name: Payments
rows.metric: Visa's payments volume passed $4tn in a quarter for the first time in fiscal Q3 2026, up 10% at constant dollars, with net revenue of $11.6bn, up 14%. Mastercard's Q2 2026 gross dollar volume was $2.9tn, up 8%, with cross-border up 12%. Stripe processed $1.9tn in 2025, up 34%.

rows.name: Digital banks and lenders
rows.metric: Customer counts are not comparable. Nubank reports about 139 million customers (secondary). Revolut cites 68 to 80 million. Chime counts 10.4 million active members, up 20%. Public markets value listed neobanks at about 4 to 5 times revenue, against Revolut's private price near 19 times (secondary estimate).

rows.name: Stablecoins and crypto
rows.metric: Stablecoin supply was about $316bn to $322bn in mid-2026 (DefiLlama-based reports). Tether held about $184bn to $190bn, around 58%, and USDC about $74bn to $79bn. The top two were 81.7% of supply. The GENIUS Act became law on 18 July 2025.

placements.key_figure: Data Center $89.0bn, quarter to 26 Jul 2026. Total revenue $96.2bn. Q3 guide $108bn.
placements.why: Sells the chips, the networking and the software together, so a customer buys one working rack.
placements.could_change: Large buyers shift volume to in-house chips, and China, where IDC has Nvidia at 34% of H1 2026 shipments.

placements.key_figure: Data Center segment $6.7bn, up 107% year on year, Q2 2026.
placements.why: Its Helios racks are deployed by Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, and two labs have signed multi-gigawatt supply deals.
placements.could_change: The MI450 class has to ship in volume in the second half of 2026 and the software has to keep pace.

placements.key_figure: 28% of China AI chip shipments in H1 2026 (572,000 units), against Nvidia's 34% (IDC, as reported).
placements.why: Its shipments nearly doubled while Nvidia's fell 44% as China steered buyers to domestic chips.
placements.could_change: Access to enough advanced manufacturing capacity to keep growing.

placements.label: newly public
placements.key_figure: IPO priced at $185 on 13 May 2026, raising $5.55bn. An OpenAI agreement valued above $20bn is cited in its S-1/A (reported).
placements.why: Builds one chip from an entire wafer, a different premise from stacking many small chips.
placements.could_change: Turning the OpenAI commitment into delivered capacity.

placements.key_figure: Non-exclusive licence of its inference technology to Nvidia (Dec 2025), reported at about $20bn. Its founder and team joined Nvidia. Groq continues as a separate company.
placements.why: Nvidia paid for low-latency inference technology it did not have.
placements.could_change: A reported Justice Department review and a Delaware stockholder suit over how the deal was structured.

placements.key_figure: $1.5bn Series E at a $6.2bn valuation, 19 Oct 2026.
placements.why: Sells open, modular AI servers to buyers who want an alternative stack.
placements.could_change: Turning the round into Galaxy server shipments and manufacturing capacity.

placements.key_figure: $500m Series B in January 2026 (CB Insights). Later offers at higher valuations are reported and unconfirmed.
placements.why: Bets that one model architecture will dominate, so a chip built only for it wins on cost.
placements.could_change: Whether transformers stay the dominant architecture.

placements.key_figure: AI semiconductor revenue $16.7bn, quarter to 2 Aug 2026. Custom accelerators were 73% of AI revenue (third-party summary).
placements.why: Co-designs the accelerators for the biggest buyers and sells the Ethernet that connects them.
placements.could_change: Customers bring more design in-house, or OpenAI's chips arrive late. Racks are planned from the second half of 2026.

placements.key_figure: Anthropic can use up to 1 million TPUs. Meta is reported to have agreed a multibillion-dollar TPU deal (Feb 2026).
placements.why: Sells its own chip capacity to rivals in AI, which gives the chip volume no single product could.
placements.could_change: Anthropic said it will keep using Amazon's Trainium and Nvidia GPUs too.

placements.key_figure: Anthropic's primary training partner (reported).
placements.why: Trainium gives AWS a cost advantage and a reason for AI labs to build on its cloud.
placements.could_change: Labs spreading workloads across several chip families.

placements.key_figure: Broadcom and Marvell are estimated to control about 95% of custom accelerator co-design (secondary estimate).
placements.why: The only other scaled partner a buyer can call.
placements.could_change: Winning a flagship program the way Broadcom won Google's.

placements.key_figure: 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed accelerators with Broadcom, under a signed term sheet. Racks planned from the second half of 2026 to the end of 2029.
placements.why: A model lab that designs its own chips can tune the hardware to its models.
placements.could_change: First silicon has to ship on schedule. Terms were not disclosed.

placements.key_figure: Q2 2026 revenue $16.1bn, up 25%. Data Center and AI $6.3bn, up 59%. x86 share 69.3%.
placements.why: Still ships about seven in ten x86 chips, and Nvidia bought $5bn of its stock and will co-develop x86 products with it.
placements.could_change: AMD keeps taking share, and 14A needs a named outside anchor customer.

placements.key_figure: x86 share 30.7%, or 34.1% with semi-custom and embedded. Server share reported near 34.5%, and it varies by definition.
placements.why: Has taken share in every segment as Intel's supply and entry-level lineup stumbled.
placements.could_change: Intel's supply recovering.

placements.key_figure: Q1 FY27 revenue $1.29bn, up 22%. Royalties $715m. Data center royalties more than doubling. Demand for its own AGI CPU above $2bn for FY27 to FY28 (company).
placements.why: Collects a royalty on most chips outside PCs, and now sells silicon of its own.
placements.could_change: Licensees object when the licensor competes with them, and RISC-V offers a way out.

placements.key_figure: Won its Nuvia licence case against Arm (Sept 2025), which Arm said it would appeal. Agreed to buy Alphawave for about $2.4bn to enter data center.
placements.why: Holds a licence it has now defended in court, and is buying connectivity IP.
placements.could_change: The appeal, and winning a data center customer.

placements.key_figure: 72.5% share, 2Q26, on about $40.2bn of revenue, up 12.1% on the quarter.
placements.why: Makes the leading-edge chips for Nvidia, Apple and most others.

placements.could_change: Converting orders into shipments.

placements.key_figure: Reported to have completed a roughly $3.25bn purchase of Celestial AI, a photonic fabric startup (single secondary source).
placements.why: Buying light-based interconnect to extend its data center position.

placements.could_change: Volume production and a major customer.

placements.why: Already sells the servers, so storage sells with them.
placements.could_change: Specialists keeping a performance lead.

placements.why: Large installed base in enterprise data.

placements.why: Fastest-growing independent, with Nvidia reported as a backer.

placements.could_change: Reaching the roughly $1bn revenue projected for 2026.

placements.why: Parallel file system built for GPU clusters.
placements.could_change: Competing with better-funded rivals.

placements.why: Large enterprise and supercomputing base.

placements.could_change: Hyperscalers building their own campuses.

placements.could_change: The A+ rated $27.3bn bond reportedly traded down to 94.4 cents (single source).

placements.key_figure: A $35bn package to buy chips for lease to Anthropic is reported as the largest private credit deal on record.

placements.could_change: Credit performance if AI demand slows.

placements.key_figure: Series F of $3.9bn at about $30.9bn post-money reported for Sept 2026.
placements.why: Builds campuses around cheap power and rents GPUs from them.
placements.could_change: Filling capacity at those prices.

placements.key_figure: Backlog $176bn at end of Q2 2026. Gas turbine backlog 44 GW in Q1 2026 and slot reservations 56 GW.

placements.could_change: Whether on-site gas becomes the fast route around grid waits.

placements.why: Sells the power and cooling inside the racks as they get denser.
placements.could_change: Liquid cooling standards and rivals' share.

placements.key_figure: Data center orders reportedly up about 200% in Q4 2025.
placements.why: Electrical gear at every step between grid and rack.
placements.could_change: Lead times and copper costs.

placements.key_figure: Fuel cell backlog near $6bn, up 140% year on year, at the start of 2026.
placements.why: Delivers power on site without waiting for the grid.
placements.could_change: Cost of gas and scale of deliveries.

placements.key_figure: 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart the Crane nuclear plant in 2027 (reported).

placements.could_change: Regulatory approvals and the restart date.

placements.could_change: Licensing and construction schedules.

placements.why: A buyer committing years ahead to a reactor design.
placements.could_change: Construction timeline.

placements.key_figure: Raised $1bn in August 2026 (Bloomberg, as reported).
placements.why: Venture money is flowing into reactor developers.
placements.could_change: Demonstrating a working reactor.

placements.could_change: Google and Microsoft growing faster from smaller bases.

placements.could_change: Capacity to serve the backlog.

placements.key_figure: Google Cloud revenue about $24.8bn in Q2 2026, up 82%, with a reported $514bn backlog (secondary coverage of Alphabet's 22 July report).

placements.could_change: Whether the backlog converts to revenue. About half is expected within 24 months.

placements.key_figure: Cloud infrastructure revenue $7.4bn in the quarter to August 2026, up 121%. Remaining performance obligations $664bn. Free cash flow was negative $5bn.
placements.why: Signed the largest AI contracts and delivered more than 300,000 GPUs since the end of May.
placements.could_change: Pre-earnings estimates put OpenAI at about half of the backlog (analyst estimate), so one customer carries much of it.

placements.key_figure: AI cloud and compute revenue 48.44bn yuan in the June 2026 quarter, up 45%. Capital spending up 75% to 67.68bn yuan (reported).
placements.why: Leads China, where US chips are restricted and domestic ones are rising.
placements.could_change: Access to enough AI chips, and Huawei and Tencent.

placements.key_figure: Q2 2026 revenue $2.575bn. Backlog about $104bn plus more than $25bn added in early Q3. Net interest expense $640m.
placements.why: Rents GPUs by the contract to buyers that cannot build fast enough, including Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft.
placements.could_change: Customer concentration (Microsoft was about 67% of 2025 revenue) and the interest bill.

placements.key_figure: Q2 revenue about $582m. Microsoft agreed to pay up to $17.4bn through 2031. Meta agreed $12bn of dedicated compute over five years, with up to $15bn more.
placements.why: Long contracts from the two biggest platform buyers.
placements.could_change: Funding: it leans on convertible debt and customer prepayments.

placements.why: A GPU cloud with a long record serving researchers.
placements.could_change: Winning a flagship contract as large as CoreWeave's.

placements.could_change: Frontier labs' models staying closed and pricing falling.

placements.could_change: Turning compute commitments into revenue. Amazon's $35bn is contingent on an IPO or an AGI milestone.

placements.why: Instruments the applications that AI labs themselves run.
placements.could_change: Customer concentration in AI-native buyers.

placements.why: Logs and security data from two budgets in one product.
placements.could_change: Whether a hardware seller can run a software subscription.

placements.could_change: Valuation conflict, and Datadog's pricing power.

placements.could_change: Part of the growth is acquired, so organic growth is lower than the headline.

placements.why: One agent and one platform, sold as a flexible credit that customers spend across modules.

placements.could_change: Chat assistants taking questions, though AI-native engines were reported under 0.1% each (single source).

placements.why: Same network economics, with strength in cross-border.

placements.why: Large user base and brand at a valuation that attracted a bid.

placements.why: Public and growing in the largest consumer banking market.

placements.why: The regulated US stablecoin, built to fit the new law.

placements.why: The largest US venue, with a growing share while the market shrank.
placements.could_change: Trading revenue is cyclical.
